english.title: Criminal damage to property - value under £5000
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful excuse,

(A)_[destroyed **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..)]_
(B)_[damaged **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..)]_

to the value of **(..SPECIFY THE VALUE UNDER FIVE THOUSAND POUNDS..) belonging to **(..SPECIFY THE NAME..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1) and (4) of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) See offence wording: H2081 - where the damage involved exceeds five thousand pounds in value.
(ii) Property damaged / destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(iii) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage is to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iv) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
(v) Low value offences - Where the value of the damage is below five thousand pounds, the offence can only be tried at a Magistrates Court. However, for all other purposes, it is still has the status of an 'either way offence'. It is possible to charge 'attempted criminal damage' of whatever value. For more on these issues, please see section 22 of the Magistrates' Court Act 1980.
(vi) There is no time limit on prosecution for this offence - even though only triable summarily, it remains an either way offence.
(vii) Penalty Notices for Disorder may only be issued to offenders aged 18 years or over. Where value of damage is below £300 this offence may be disposed of by the issue of a Penalty Notice for Disorder- PND Code DA11 - but a PND should not be issued to an offender who is a substance mis-user. Where a PND is issued it should be recorded on PNC within 24 hours - according to ACPO guidelines.
(vii) Where the damage is to a memorial (see section 22(11A) and (11D)) the value of the damage is irrelevant to mode of trial and the offence can be tried summarily or on indictment even if the value involved is less than £5000, see section 22(1) of, and Schedule 2 to, the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.
